IDN.note: GAPKI 2024 (calendar year): CPO production 48.16 Mt; palm-oil-product exports 29.54 Mt; domestic use rose with the B35/B40 biodiesel mandate. World's largest producer and exporter.

MYS.note: MPOB 2024 (calendar year): crude palm oil production 19.3 Mt, palm oil exports 16.9 Mt. Malaysia also imports ~1 Mt of Indonesian CPO for refining/re-export. World #2 producer and exporter.

THA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: production ~3.3 Mt, mostly consumed domestically (food + biodiesel); exportable surplus ~0.4-0.6 Mt. World's #3 palm-oil exporter.

COL.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: Latin America's largest producer (~1.85 Mt); exports ~0.75 Mt to EU, Mexico, Brazil. EUDR-compliant lower-deforestation-risk origin.

GTM.note: Largest Central American palm-oil exporter; EU imported 396 kt from Guatemala in 2024 (WITS). Total exports ~0.8 Mt to EU and Mexico.

HND.note: Honduras exported 202 kt to the EU alone in 2024 (WITS); total exports ~0.35 Mt to EU and Mexico.

PNG.note: RSPO-certified exporter; EU imported 285 kt and India 185 kt from PNG in 2024 (WITS). Nearly all output exported.

IND.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: India imported 8,620 kt of palm oil (HS 1511) — the world's largest importer. Indonesia 4,596 + Malaysia 2,924 + Thailand 753 + PNG 185 kt main suppliers.

CHN.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: China imported 3,665 kt of palm oil — Indonesia 2,443 + Malaysia 1,213 kt are ~99.7% of supply. World's #2 importer.

EU.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: EU-27 imported 3,821 kt of palm oil (extra-EU) — Indonesia 1,393 + Malaysia 995, with Guatemala 396, PNG 285, Honduras 202, Colombia 77 kt diversifying ahead of EUDR.

PAK.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Pakistan imported 3,093 kt of palm oil — Indonesia 2,729 (~88%) + Malaysia 363 kt. World's #4 importer; palm oil is the staple cooking fat.

BGD.note: Bangladesh did NOT report HS 1511 imports to UN Comtrade for 2024. USDA PSD MY2024/25: ~1.45 Mt imports, overwhelmingly Indonesia/Malaysia. Carried on USDA basis.

EGY.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Egypt imported 891 kt of palm oil — Indonesia 581 + Malaysia 309 kt (~99.8%). Major MENA buyer.

USA.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: US imported 1,749 kt of palm oil — Indonesia 1,535 (~88%) + Malaysia 164 kt. Subject to CBP forced-labour withhold-release actions on some Malaysian suppliers.

PHL.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Philippines imported 1,079 kt of palm oil — Malaysia 660 + Indonesia 411 kt. One of few large markets where Malaysia outsells Indonesia.

KEN.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Kenya imported 875 kt of palm oil — Malaysia 778 (~89%) + Indonesia 95 kt. East African import-and-refining hub, re-exporting to Uganda, Tanzania, DRC.

TUR.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: Turkey imports ~1 Mt palm oil, mainly Indonesia/Malaysia. 2024 HS 1511 importer return incomplete on WITS, carried on USDA basis.

VNM.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: Vietnam imports ~1 Mt palm oil, almost entirely Indonesia/Malaysia. Non-reporter, carried on USDA basis.

NGA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: Nigeria is Africa's largest producer (~1.4 Mt) but still net importer (~0.6 Mt, much informal). Comtrade return partial, USDA basis.

MMR.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: Myanmar imports ~0.7 Mt palm oil, almost all Malaysia/Indonesia. Reporting unreliable, USDA basis.

SAU.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: Saudi imports ~0.65 Mt palm oil from Indonesia/Malaysia for food manufacturing and Gulf re-export. WITS 2024 incomplete, USDA basis.

IRQ.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: Iraq imports ~0.6 Mt palm oil, mainly Indonesia/Malaysia (some via UAE re-export). Non-reporter, USDA basis.

companies.name: Wilmar International
companies.metric: Revenue ≈ US$67bn (FY2024); world's largest palm-oil processor and trader.
companies.note: Asia's leading agribusiness; integrated from plantations through refining, branded consumer oils and oleochemicals.
companies.improve: Should publish mill-level, fully-traceable-to-plantation coverage and grievance-case resolution rates rather than aggregate NDPE commitments.

companies.name: SD Guthrie (Sime Darby Plantation)
companies.metric: World's largest oil-palm plantation company by planted area; revenue ≈ US$4-4.5bn (FY2024). Rebranded SD Guthrie in 2024.
companies.note: RSPO-certified across operations; major CPO and downstream producer.
companies.improve: Should keep publishing third-party labour-audit results and plantation-level GHG/peat emissions to keep US/EU market access secure.

companies.name: Golden Agri-Resources (GAR)
companies.metric: ~US$10-11bn revenue (FY2024); Sinar Mas group; largest planted area in Indonesia.
companies.note: Heavily concentrated in Indonesia; integrated to refining, branded oils and biodiesel feedstock.
companies.improve: Near-total Indonesia concentration exposes it to policy swings; should report concession-level peat and fire-hotspot data.

companies.name: IOI Corporation
companies.metric: Revenue ≈ US$2.5-3bn (FY2024); strong in specialty oleochemicals and refined palm products.
companies.note: Plantations plus a large downstream specialty-fats and oleochemical arm.
companies.improve: Should disclose the deforestation-free share of its downstream specialty-fats feedstock, which buyers increasingly demand.

companies.name: Musim Mas
companies.metric: One of the largest privately-held palm-oil groups; fully integrated across plantations, refining, oleochemicals.
companies.note: Privately owned; key supplier to consumer-goods majors; early mover on smallholder traceability in Indonesia.
companies.improve: Should voluntarily publish mill-level traceability coverage and an EUDR-compliance roadmap given heavy smallholder supply.

companies.name: FGV Holdings
companies.metric: Malaysia's largest CPO producer by volume (Felda smallholder scheme); revenue ≈ US$5bn (FY2024).
companies.note: Central to the Felda smallholder-settler model.
companies.improve: Sustaining market access requires continued independent labour audits and settler-level traceability and income data.

global.note: World palm oil totals, kt, USDA FAS PSD. Production past ~79 Mt by 2024 (Indonesia ~47-48 Mt + Malaysia ~19 Mt = ~85%). Exports plateaued near ~50 Mt as Indonesia's B35/B40 biodiesel mandate absorbed a rising share domestically. Trade detail uses WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (HS 1511), excludes palm kernel oil (HS 1513).

forecast.method: Projected 2030 = 2024 × (1 + rate)^6, inside the OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook envelope: output growth slowing to ~1.5%/yr as yields plateau; trade growth softer (~1%/yr) because Indonesia's biodiesel mandates absorb supply.
